record.original_question: For every generalized minimal flow u(x,t) in two-dimensional Euler dynamics, are all level lines of the vorticity curl u(x,t)=constant real analytic?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equations on a domain in $\mathbb{R}^2$ (or on the two-torus), governing a divergence-free velocity field $u(x,t)$ with vorticity $\omega(x,t) = \operatorname{curl} u(x,t) = \partial_1 u_2 - \partial_2 u_1$. A "generalized minimal flow" (GM-flow) is a solution $u(x,t)$ obtained as a critical point (in the appropriate generalized/relaxed sense) of the kinetic-energy functional restricted to the coadjoint orbit of the initial vorticity under the action of the volume-preserving diffeomorphism group; equivalently, it is a steady or relaxed steady state of the 2D Euler equations realized as a minimizer of the $L^2$ kinetic energy among rearrangements of a prescribed vorticity profile.

Prove or disprove: for every such generalized minimal flow $u(x,t)$, every level set $\{x : \omega(x,t) = c\}$ of the vorticity is a real-analytic curve (where defined).
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution of this specific question about real-analyticity of vorticity level sets for generalized minimal flows of 2D Euler was found. Related work studies analytic structure of stationary 2D Euler flows and stream-function level sets, but the conjecture for arbitrary GM-flows appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Analytic Structure of Stationary Flows of an Ideal Fluid with a Stagnation Point
status_evidence.snippet: Studies analytic structure of stationary 2D Euler flows and level lines of the stream function corresponding to flow lines.
status_evidence.claim: Related stationary-flow analyticity results exist but do not resolve the GM-flow problem in full generality.
